claim: Base editors can generate C-to-T point mutations with high efficiencies without other unwanted on-target mutations in zebrafish.
source: Here we show that base editors can generate C-to-T point mutations with high efficiencies without other unwanted on-target mutations.
evidence: The abstract directly states this finding, which is supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript showing editing efficiencies and absence of INDELs.

claim: A new editor variant recognizing an NAA protospacer adjacent motif was established, expanding base editing possibilities in zebrafish.
source: In addition, we established a new editor variant recognizing an NAA protospacer adjacent motif, expanding the base editing possibilities in zebrafish.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this achievement, which is demonstrated experimentally in the Results section with the ancBE4max-SpymacCas9 variant.

claim: A base change was generated in the ctnnb1 gene, mimicking an oncogenic mutation of the human gene known to result in constitutive activation of endogenous Wnt signaling.
source: Using these approaches, we first generated a base change in the ctnnb1 gene, mimicking oncogenic an mutation of the human gene known to result in constitutive activation of endogenous Wnt signaling.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by experimental data showing GFP activation in Wnt reporter embryos and sequencing data confirming the S33L mutation.

claim: Several cancer-associated genes including cbl were precisely targeted using base editing.
source: Additionally, we precisely targeted several cancer-associated genes including cbl.
evidence: The abstract states this, and the manuscript provides sequencing data and editing efficiencies for multiple cancer-associated genes.

claim: A new zebrafish dwarfism model was created by targeting the cbl gene.
source: With this last target, we created a new zebrafish dwarfism model.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by phenotypic data showing reduced body size in MZ cbl−/− mutants.

claim: The CRISPR/Cas9 system enables rapid and efficient generation of loss-of-function mutations in zebrafish.
source: The CRISPR (clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats)/Cas9 system is indeed a remarkably powerful gene-editing tool (Sander and Joung, 2014) that enables the rapid and efficient generation of loss-of-function mutations in this animal model.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Sander and Joung, 2014, indicating it draws from established literature.

claim: The CRISPR/Cas9 system relies on specific binding of a sgRNA-Cas9 complex that interacts with DNA 20 base pairs upstream of an NGG protospacer adjacent motif sequence.
source: This system relies on the specific binding of a sgRNA-Cas9 complex that initially interacts with DNA 20 base pair (bp) upstream of a NGG protospacer adjacent motif (PAM) sequence that triggers the Cas9 protein to introduce a double-strand break (DSB).
evidence: This describes the established mechanism of CRISPR/Cas9, drawing from general scientific knowledge about the system.

claim: CRISPR/Cas9 is widely used in zebrafish to produce knock-out alleles.
source: This technique is nowadays widely used in zebrafish notably to produce knock-out alleles (Hwang et al., 2013), and more recently, it has also been demonstrated that CRISPR/Cas9-mediated homology-directed repair (HDR) can be used to introduce exogenous DNA and single-nucleotide polymorphisms (Prykhozhij et al., 2018; Tessadori et al., 2018; Wierson et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published work demonstrating these applications.

claim: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated homology-directed repair can be used to introduce exogenous DNA and single-nucleotide polymorphisms in zebrafish.
source: This technique is nowadays widely used in zebrafish notably to produce knock-out alleles (Hwang et al., 2013), and more recently, it has also been demonstrated that CRISPR/Cas9-mediated homology-directed repair (HDR) can be used to introduce exogenous DNA and single-nucleotide polymorphisms (Prykhozhij et al., 2018; Tessadori et al., 2018; Wierson et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to three recent publications demonstrating HDR applications in zebrafish.

claim: A CRISPR/Cas9-based technology has been developed to precisely edit single bases of DNA without introducing DSBs in human cells.
source: Recently, a CRISPR/Cas9-based technology has been developed to precisely edit single bases of DNA without introducing DSBs in human cells (Koblan et al., 2018; Komor et al., 2016; Komor et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to publications describing base editing technology in human cells.

claim: The base editing method is based on the fusion of a Cas9-D10A nickase with a cytidine deaminase giving rise to a cytidine base editor (CBE).
source: The method is based on the fusion of a Cas9-D10A nickase with a cytidine deaminase giving rise to a cytidine base editor (CBE).
evidence: This describes the established mechanism of CBE technology, drawing from scientific knowledge about base editors.

claim: CBE converts C-to-T bases in a restricted window of 13–19 nucleotides upstream of the PAM sequence.
source: CBE converts C-to-T bases in a restricted window of 13–19 nucleotides (nt) upstream of the PAM sequence (Figure 1A).
evidence: This statement describes the mechanism of CBE and references Figure 1A which illustrates this concept.

claim: In zebrafish, a CBE was shown to work but with limited efficiencies, inducing less than 29% of gene editing.
source: In zebrafish, a CBE was shown to work but with limited efficiencies, inducing less than 29% of gene editing and, in most cases, at least 5% of unwanted INDEL (insertion or deletion) mutations were also detected (Carrington et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous zebrafish base editing studies.

claim: First generation CBEs in zebrafish produced at least 5% of unwanted INDEL mutations in most cases.
source: In zebrafish, a CBE was shown to work but with limited efficiencies, inducing less than 29% of gene editing and, in most cases, at least 5% of unwanted INDEL (insertion or deletion) mutations were also detected (Carrington et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies reporting INDEL formation with early CBE variants.

claim: Several studies in cell culture have optimized and engineered new base editor variants with increased gene-editing efficiency reaching up to 90% without creating undesired INDEL mutations.
source: However, since this first generation of CBEs, several studies in cell culture have optimized and engineered new base editor variants with increased gene-editing efficiency reaching up to 90% without creating undesired INDEL mutations (Koblan et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Koblan et al., 2018 describing improved base editor variants.

claim: A recent study reported the use of a second-generation CBE to generate a zebrafish model of human ablepharon macrostomia syndrome.
source: A recent study reported the use of a second-generation CBE to generate a zebrafish model of human ablepharon macrostomia syndrome (Zhao et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Zhao et al., 2020.

claim: Upon ctnnb1 S33L sgRNA injection with BE4-gam, an increase of GFP-positive cells was observed at 1 dpf in 39 of 50 embryos compared to 27 control embryos.
source: Upon ctnnb1 S33L sgRNA injection, we observed an increase of GFP-positive cells at 1 dpf (n = 39/50 embryos) compared to the control embryos (n = 27 embryos) resulting from three independent experiments.
evidence: This statement reports experimental data from injected embryos showing Wnt pathway activation.

claim: An average of 12 GFP-positive clones per retina were observed in ctnnb1 S33L sgRNA injected embryos, while GFP-positive cells were never detected in the retina of control injected embryos.
source: By confocal imaging we quantified ectopic activation of the pathway in retinal progenitor cells and observed an average of 12 GFP-positive clones per retina, while GFP-positive cells were never detected in the retina of control injected Tg(7xTCF-Xla.Siam:GFP) embryos (n = 4 each) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This reports quantified imaging data from confocal microscopy experiments, with reference to Figure 1B.

claim: Base editing was observed in five of eight randomly chosen embryos for ctnnb1 targeting with BE4-gam.
source: Using this strategy, we observed base editing in five of eight randomly chosen embryos and were able to reach up to 73% of editing efficiency in single embryo analysis (Table 1, Table 2).
evidence: This reports experimental data on editing efficiency from sequencing analysis.

claim: Up to 73% of editing efficiency was reached in single embryo analysis for ctnnb1 targeting with BE4-gam.
source: Using this strategy, we observed base editing in five of eight randomly chosen embryos and were able to reach up to 73% of editing efficiency in single embryo analysis (Table 1, Table 2).
evidence: This reports quantified editing efficiency data from Sanger sequencing analysis.

claim: Conversion of another cytidine within the PAM [−19, –13 bp] window leading to a silent mutation (GAC-to-GAT (D)) was observed in four of eight analyzed embryos with up to 74% efficiency for ctnnb1 targeting.
source: In addition, we also observed the conversion of another cytidine within the PAM [−19, –13 bp] window leading to a silent mutation (GAC-to-GAT (D)) in four of the eight analyzed embryos with up to 74% efficiency (Figure 1C, Table 1, Table 2, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This reports experimental sequencing data showing an additional C-to-T conversion at the targeted locus.

claim: The mutation of Serine33 of human β-catenin protein into a Leucine prevents its degradation by the ubiquitin-proteasome system, leading to its stabilization and constitutive activation of Wnt signaling pathway.
source: It was previously shown that the mutation of the Serine33 of the human β-catenin protein into a Leucine prevents its degradation by the ubiquitin-proteasome system, leading to its stabilization and thereby to the constitutive activation of Wnt signaling pathway (Hart et al., 1999; Liu et al., 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Hart et al., 1999 and Liu et al., 1999.

claim: Q94* mutation in Tek was induced in five of eight randomly chosen embryos using BE4-gam.
source: We induced the Q94* mutation in Tek in five of eight randomly chosen embryos, Q273* mutation in Bap1 in four of eight randomly chosen embryos and Q21* mutation in p53 in six of eight randomly chosen embryos as well as Q170* in p53 in seven of eight randomly chosen embryos by C-to-T conversions (Figure 1D–G, Table 1, Table 2).
evidence: This reports experimental data from sequencing analysis of injected embryos.

claim: Q273* mutation in Bap1 was induced in four of eight randomly chosen embryos using BE4-gam.
source: We induced the Q94* mutation in Tek in five of eight randomly chosen embryos, Q273* mutation in Bap1 in four of eight randomly chosen embryos and Q21* mutation in p53 in six of eight randomly chosen embryos as well as Q170* in p53 in seven of eight randomly chosen embryos by C-to-T conversions (Figure 1D–G, Table 1, Table 2).
evidence: This reports experimental data from sequencing analysis of injected embryos.

claim: Q21* mutation in p53 was induced in six of eight randomly chosen embryos using BE4-gam.
source: We induced the Q94* mutation in Tek in five of eight randomly chosen embryos, Q273* mutation in Bap1 in four of eight randomly chosen embryos and Q21* mutation in p53 in six of eight randomly chosen embryos as well as Q170* in p53 in seven of eight randomly chosen embryos by C-to-T conversions (Figure 1D–G, Table 1, Table 2).
evidence: This reports experimental data from sequencing analysis of injected embryos.

claim: Q170* mutation in p53 was induced in seven of eight randomly chosen embryos using BE4-gam.
source: We induced the Q94* mutation in Tek in five of eight randomly chosen embryos, Q273* mutation in Bap1 in four of eight randomly chosen embryos and Q21* mutation in p53 in six of eight randomly chosen embryos as well as Q170* in p53 in seven of eight randomly chosen embryos by C-to-T conversions (Figure 1D–G, Table 1, Table 2).
evidence: This reports experimental data from sequencing analysis of injected embryos.

claim: Up to 86% of C-to-T conversion was reached for the introduction of the Q170* mutation in tp53 using BE4-gam.
source: Among the different targeted mutations, the highest efficiency was achieved with the tp53 tumor suppressor gene, for which we reached up to 86% of C-to-T conversion for the introduction of the Q170* mutation (Figure 1G, Table 1, Table 2).
evidence: This reports quantified editing efficiency data from sequencing analysis.

claim: For tek targeting with BE4-gam, 6 of 20 clones showed precise C-to-T conversions, while all other analyzed sequences were wild type without any error or INDEL formation.
source: For tek 6 of 20, bap1 2 of 12, tp53 (Q21*) 12 of 24, and lastly tp53 (Q170*) 21 of 24 colonies showed precise C-to-T conversions, whereas all the other analyzed sequences were wild type, without any error or INDEL formation.
evidence: This reports experimental data from clonal sequencing analysis assessing editing precision.

claim: For bap1 targeting with BE4-gam, 2 of 12 clones showed precise C-to-T conversions, while all other analyzed sequences were wild type without any error or INDEL formation.
source: For tek 6 of 20, bap1 2 of 12, tp53 (Q21*) 12 of 24, and lastly tp53 (Q170*) 21 of 24 colonies showed precise C-to-T conversions, whereas all the other analyzed sequences were wild type, without any error or INDEL formation.
evidence: This reports experimental data from clonal sequencing analysis assessing editing precision.

claim: For tp53 (Q21*) targeting with BE4-gam, 12 of 24 clones showed precise C-to-T conversions, while all other analyzed sequences were wild type without any error or INDEL formation.
source: For tek 6 of 20, bap1 2 of 12, tp53 (Q21*) 12 of 24, and lastly tp53 (Q170*) 21 of 24 colonies showed precise C-to-T conversions, whereas all the other analyzed sequences were wild type, without any error or INDEL formation.
evidence: This reports experimental data from clonal sequencing analysis assessing editing precision.

claim: For tp53 (Q170*) targeting with BE4-gam, 21 of 24 clones showed precise C-to-T conversions, while all other analyzed sequences were wild type without any error or INDEL formation.
source: For tek 6 of 20, bap1 2 of 12, tp53 (Q21*) 12 of 24, and lastly tp53 (Q170*) 21 of 24 colonies showed precise C-to-T conversions, whereas all the other analyzed sequences were wild type, without any error or INDEL formation.
evidence: This reports experimental data from clonal sequencing analysis assessing editing precision.

claim: The ancBE4max CBE variant has been engineered and optimized in cell culture with increased efficiency compared to BE4-gam, reaching up to 90% efficiency and very low rates of INDELs.
source: More recently, a new CBE variant, the ancBE4max, has been engineered and optimized in cell culture with increased efficiency compared to the classical BE4-gam, reaching up to 90% efficiency and very low rates of INDELs (Koblan et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Koblan et al., 2018 describing the ancBE4max variant.

claim: No C-to-T conversions or other unwanted changes were obtained using BE4-gam for kras E62K targeting in eight randomly chosen embryos.
source: We therefore decided to use this new CBE variant to target the oncogenic mutation E62K in Kras and induce the creation of a Q8* stop codon in the Dmd tumor suppressor for which we did not obtain any C-to-T conversions or other unwanted changes using the BE4-gam in randomly chosen eight embryos for each condition (Table 1, Table 2).
evidence: This reports experimental data showing lack of editing with BE4-gam for specific targets.

claim: No C-to-T conversions or other unwanted changes were obtained using BE4-gam for dmd Q8* targeting in eight randomly chosen embryos.
source: We therefore decided to use this new CBE variant to target the oncogenic mutation E62K in Kras and induce the creation of a Q8* stop codon in the Dmd tumor suppressor for which we did not obtain any C-to-T conversions or other unwanted changes using the BE4-gam in randomly chosen eight embryos for each condition (Table 1, Table 2).
evidence: This reports experimental data showing lack of editing with BE4-gam for specific targets.

claim: By co-injection of ancBE4max mRNA with kras E62K sgRNA, the E62K mutation was introduced in four of seven randomly chosen embryos with up to 19% editing efficiency.
source: By co-injection of ancBE4max mRNA with the kras E62K sgRNA, we were able to introduce the E62K mutation in four of seven randomly chosen embryos and we were able to reach up to 19% of editing efficiency in single embryo analysis.
evidence: This reports experimental data from sequencing analysis showing editing with ancBE4max.

claim: Another cytidine in the editing window was converted during kras E62K targeting with ancBE4max, leading to a silent mutation (CAG-to-CAA (Q)).
source: Another cytidine in the editing window was also converted and led to the generation of a silent mutation (CAG-to-CAA (Q)) (Figure 2A, Table 1, Table 2).
evidence: This reports experimental sequencing data showing an additional C-to-T conversion.

claim: A Q8* mutation in Dmd was obtained in two of four randomly chosen embryos with up to 14% editing efficiency using ancBE4max.
source: Similar to what we observed in the case of kras editing, we were able to obtain a Q8* mutation in the Dmd tumor suppressor in two of four randomly chosen embryos with up to 14% of editing efficiency (Figure 2B, Table 1, Table 2).
evidence: This reports experimental data from sequencing analysis showing editing with ancBE4max.

claim: For sod2 targeting with ancBE4max, up to 64% editing efficiency was reached and 100% of sequenced embryos (n=8) were precisely mutated.
source: Remarkable editing efficiency was also observed using this CBE for two additional targets: the tumor suppressor genes sod2 and rb1, for which, respectively, up to 64% and 91% of editing were reached and 100% of the sequenced embryos were precisely mutated (from single embryo analysis of n = 8 randomly analyzed embryos) (Figure 2C,D, Table 1, Table 2; Bravard et al., 1992; Dyson, 2016).
evidence: This reports experimental data from sequencing analysis showing high editing efficiency with ancBE4max.

claim: For rb1 targeting with ancBE4max, up to 91% editing efficiency was reached and 100% of sequenced embryos (n=8) were precisely mutated.
source: Remarkable editing efficiency was also observed using this CBE for two additional targets: the tumor suppressor genes sod2 and rb1, for which, respectively, up to 64% and 91% of editing were reached and 100% of the sequenced embryos were precisely mutated (from single embryo analysis of n = 8 randomly analyzed embryos) (Figure 2C,D, Table 1, Table 2; Bravard et al., 1992; Dyson, 2016).
evidence: This reports experimental data from sequencing analysis showing high editing efficiency with ancBE4max.

claim: All cytidine bases present in the PAM [−19, –13] bp window can be edited by the CBE, with higher efficiency for cytidine bases located in the middle of this window.
source: It is interesting to note that in general all the cytidine bases present in the PAM [−19, –13] bp window can be edited by the CBE, with a higher efficiency for the cytidine bases located in the middle of this window while editing was below detection levels for cytidines located only 12 bp upstream (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data showing differential editing efficiencies at different positions, as shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Editing was below detection levels for cytidines located only 12 bp upstream of the PAM.
source: It is interesting to note that in general all the cytidine bases present in the PAM [−19, –13] bp window can be edited by the CBE, with a higher efficiency for the cytidine bases located in the middle of this window while editing was below detection levels for cytidines located only 12 bp upstream (Figure 2D).
evidence: This reports experimental observation from sequencing data showing position-dependent editing efficiency.

claim: The cytidine distance from the PAM is important for efficient editing in zebrafish.
source: With the use of ancBE4max CBE, these results highlight the importance of the cytidine distance from the PAM for efficient editing in zebrafish as shown previously in cell culture assays (Gaudelli et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data supported by a citation to previous cell culture work.

claim: The PIM domain of SpCas9 was replaced with that of SpymacCas9 in the ancBE4max to create ancBE4max-SpymacCas9.
source: To this end, we replaced the PAM-interacting motif (PIM) domain of the SpCas9 with the one of the SpymacCas9 in the ancBE4max (Jakimo et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes the molecular cloning strategy used to generate the new editor variant, supported by a citation.

claim: The inserted PIM domain in ancBE4max-SpymacCas9 was codon optimized for zebrafish.
source: The inserted PIM domain was codon optimized for zebrafish.
evidence: This describes a methodological detail of the construct generation.

claim: Using ancBE4max-SpymacCas9, the human G13S mutation in Nras oncogene was reproduced in zebrafish in 2 out of 4 randomly analyzed embryos with up to 19% efficiency.
source: Using this newly generated ancBE4max-SpymacCas9, we were able to reproduce the human G13S mutation in Nras oncogene in zebrafish in 2 out of 4 randomly analyzed embryo with up to 19% of efficiency reached in single embryo analysis (Figure 2E, Table 1, Table 2).
evidence: This reports experimental data from sequencing analysis showing editing with the new NAA PAM-recognizing editor.

claim: A stop codon was introduced by C-to-T conversion in the tp53 gene in 1 out of 4 randomly analyzed embryos with 16% efficiency using ancBE4max-SpymacCas9.
source: We also introduced a stop codon by a C-to-T conversion in the tp53 gene in 1 out of 4 randomly analyzed embryo with 16% efficiency (Figure 2F, Table 1, Table 2).
evidence: This reports experimental data from sequencing analysis showing editing with the NAA PAM-recognizing editor.

claim: It is now possible to target NAA PAMs in zebrafish in addition to the classical NGG PAM.
source: These results demonstrate that in addition to the classical NGG PAM it is now also possible to target NAA PAMs in zebrafish, thereby significantly expanding the range of cytidine bases that can be converted.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing successful editing with the SpymacCas9 variant.

claim: Genetic alterations that lead to oncogene activation and/or tumor suppressor inactivation are responsible for tumorigenesis.
source: Genetic alterations that lead to oncogene activation and/or tumor suppressor inactivation are responsible for tumorigenesis.
evidence: This statement reflects established scientific knowledge about cancer biology.

claim: In cancer patients, a series of genetic mutations in tumor suppressor genes and/or oncogenes are combined to lead to the appearance of the disease.
source: It is indeed well-established that in cancer patients, a series of genetic mutations in tumor suppressor genes and/or oncogenes are combined to all together lead to the appearance of the disease (Dash et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Dash et al., 2019 and reflects established cancer biology knowledge.

claim: Cbl is an E3 ubiquitin ligase that is found mutated in Noonan syndrome patients presenting short stature and other bone malformations.
source: Among the chosen loci to test the efficiency of the BE4-gam, we targeted the tumor suppressor gene encoding for Cbl, an E3 ubiquitin ligase, that is found mutated in Noonan syndrome patients presenting short stature and other bone malformations among several other phenotypes (Martinelli et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Martinelli et al., 2010.

claim: Activating mutations in the fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3) gene are a leading cause of dwarfism achondroplasia and related dwarf conditions.
source: In human, activating mutations in the fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3) gene are a leading cause of dwarfism achondroplasia and related dwarf conditions.
evidence: This statement reflects established knowledge about human genetic disorders.

claim: FGFR3 hyperactivation triggers intracellular signaling within the chondrocytes of the growth plate which terminates its proliferation and bone growth.
source: Indeed, FGFR3 hyperactivation triggers intracellular signaling within the chondrocytes of the growth plate which terminates its proliferation and bone growth (Harada et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Harada et al., 2009.

claim: Some activating mutations in FGFR3 disrupt c-Cbl-mediated ubiquitination that serves as a targeting signal for lysosomal degradation and termination of receptor signaling.
source: Interestingly, another study based on in vitro systems reported that some of these activating mutations in FGFR3 disrupt c-Cbl-mediated ubiquitination that serves as a targeting signal for lysosomal degradation and termination of receptor signaling (Cho et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Cho et al., 2004 describing in vitro findings.

claim: Up to 50% gene-editing efficiency was obtained for cbl targeting with BE4-gam.
source: Using the CBE BE4-gam as previously described, we obtained up to 50% of gene-editing efficiency (Figure 3A, Table 1, Table 2), with 80% of the analyzed embryos showing the expected editing (n = 10 randomly analyzed embryos).
evidence: This reports experimental data from sequencing analysis of cbl-targeted embryos.

claim: 80% of analyzed embryos (n=10) showed expected editing for cbl targeting with BE4-gam.
source: Using the CBE BE4-gam as previously described, we obtained up to 50% of gene-editing efficiency (Figure 3A, Table 1, Table 2), with 80% of the analyzed embryos showing the expected editing (n = 10 randomly analyzed embryos).
evidence: This reports experimental data from sequencing analysis of cbl-targeted embryos.

claim: Four of 15 adults carried the Cbl W577* mutation in germ cells.
source: Four of 15 adults carried the Cbl W577* mutation in germ cells and one of these carriers transmitted it to 28% of its F1 offspring (44 of 153 analyzed fish carried the mutation).
evidence: This reports experimental data from genotyping of adult fish and their offspring.

claim: One carrier of the Cbl W577* mutation transmitted it to 28% of its F1 offspring (44 of 153 analyzed fish).
source: Four of 15 adults carried the Cbl W577* mutation in germ cells and one of these carriers transmitted it to 28% of its F1 offspring (44 of 153 analyzed fish carried the mutation).
evidence: This reports experimental data from genotyping of F1 offspring.

claim: No INDELs were found in the F1 embryos carrying the cbl mutation.
source: The target sequence was analyzed in the F1 embryos and no INDELs were found (Figure 3B).
evidence: This reports experimental data from sequencing analysis of F1 embryos.

claim: Zygotic homozygous cbl mutant fish (cbl−/−) did not develop any obvious phenotype and could be grown to adulthood.
source: The zygotic homozygous mutant fish (cbl−/−) deriving from the incross of two heterozygous parents (cbl+/−) did not develop any obvious phenotype and could be grown to adulthood.
evidence: This reports experimental observation of fish phenotypes.

claim: Maternal factors stored as mRNAs and proteins in the egg can compensate for zygotic loss of function during embryonic stages in zebrafish.
source: This could be due to the fact that in zebrafish, maternal factors stored as mRNAs and proteins in the egg can compensate for zygotic loss of function during embryonic stages.
evidence: This is an inference based on established knowledge about maternal contribution in zebrafish development.

claim: 24% of MZ cbl−/− mutants displayed significantly reduced overall growth and size by 3 months post-fertilization.
source: Interestingly, 24% of the MZ cbl−/− mutants displayed a significantly reduced overall growth and size by 3 months post-fertilization, while 100% of the progeny of the cbl+/+ sibling fish showed a normal body size (means: 2.7 cm for the wild-type controls and 1.96 cm for the dwarf MZ cbl−/−, Figure 3C,D).
evidence: This reports experimental data from phenotypic analysis and body size measurements.

claim: 100% of the progeny of cbl+/+ sibling fish showed normal body size at 3 months post-fertilization.
source: Interestingly, 24% of the MZ cbl−/− mutants displayed a significantly reduced overall growth and size by 3 months post-fertilization, while 100% of the progeny of the cbl+/+ sibling fish showed a normal body size (means: 2.7 cm for the wild-type controls and 1.96 cm for the dwarf MZ cbl−/−, Figure 3C,D).
evidence: This reports experimental data from phenotypic analysis and body size measurements.

claim: The mean body length was 2.7 cm for wild-type controls and 1.96 cm for dwarf MZ cbl−/− at 3 months post-fertilization.
source: Interestingly, 24% of the MZ cbl−/− mutants displayed a significantly reduced overall growth and size by 3 months post-fertilization, while 100% of the progeny of the cbl+/+ sibling fish showed a normal body size (means: 2.7 cm for the wild-type controls and 1.96 cm for the dwarf MZ cbl−/−, Figure 3C,D).
evidence: This reports quantified experimental data from body size measurements.

claim: The dwarf phenotype was never observed in any fish derived from incrosses of wild-type stocks used to generate the cbl mutant line.
source: Furthermore, this dwarf phenotype was never observed in any of the fish derived from the incrosses of the wild-type stocks used to generate this mutant line, while it was observed in the progeny of two other crosses of the cbl−/− line.
evidence: This reports experimental observation from control crosses.

claim: The dwarf phenotype was observed in the progeny of two other crosses of the cbl−/− line.
source: Furthermore, this dwarf phenotype was never observed in any of the fish derived from the incrosses of the wild-type stocks used to generate this mutant line, while it was observed in the progeny of two other crosses of the cbl−/− line.
evidence: This reports experimental observation supporting reproducibility of the phenotype.

claim: Four germline mutations located in the RING domain of Cbl (Q367P, K382E, D390Y, and R420Q) have been previously identified and associated with Noonan syndrome and related phenotypes.
source: Four germline mutations located in the RING domain of Cbl (Q367P, K382E, D390Y, and R420Q) have been previously identified and associated to Noonan syndrome and related phenotypes (Martinelli et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Martinelli et al., 2010.

claim: The results with the cbl mutant are in line with growth defect phenotypes observed in Noonan syndrome patients.
source: Our results are in line with the growth defect phenotypes observed in these patients and directly implicate Cbl loss-of-function as a cause of bone malformations in an animal model.
evidence: This is an inference connecting the experimental phenotype to human disease phenotypes.

claim: The cbl mutant results directly implicate Cbl loss-of-function as a cause of bone malformations in an animal model.
source: Our results are in line with the growth defect phenotypes observed in these patients and directly implicate Cbl loss-of-function as a cause of bone malformations in an animal model.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental phenotypic data.

claim: A point mutation in zebrafish Cbl (H382Y) has been implicated in myeloproliferative disorders.
source: In addition, a point mutation in zebrafish Cbl (H382Y) has been implicated in myeloproliferative disorders.
evidence: This statement reflects knowledge from previous zebrafish studies.

claim: cblH382Y mutant fish do not survive to adulthood.
source: Unlike our mutant, cblH382Y mutant fish do not survive to adulthood, suggesting that the CblW577* premature stop reported here may have different consequences on the multiple functions of Cbl (Peng et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Peng et al., 2015.

claim: The CblW577* premature stop may have different consequences on the multiple functions of Cbl compared to the CblH382Y mutation.
source: Unlike our mutant, cblH382Y mutant fish do not survive to adulthood, suggesting that the CblW577* premature stop reported here may have different consequences on the multiple functions of Cbl (Peng et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a speculative inference comparing two different mutations and their phenotypic consequences.

claim: Base editors achieved highly efficient C-to-T conversion, reaching up to 91% efficiency without unwanted mutations.
source: As reported in ex vivo studies (Koblan et al., 2018), we tested different CBE variants and obtained highly efficient C-to-T conversion, reaching up to 91% efficiency without unwanted mutations and expanded base editing possibilities using a CBE variant recognizing the NAA PAM.
evidence: This summarizes experimental findings from the study, supported by data in tables and figures, and references prior work.

claim: Previous work reported a maximum efficiency of 29% using BE3 in zebrafish.
source: In comparison, previous work has reported an efficiency reaching a maximum of 29% using the BE3 (Zhang et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2017.

claim: Differences in efficiency between studies might be due to the choice of specific locus targeted, synthesis of sgRNA, and injection mode.
source: Another more recent study employed the ancBE4max variant in zebrafish with a slight difference of efficiency that might be due to the choice of the specific locus targeted, the synthesis of the sgRNA (homemade vs commercially synthetized) and the injection mode (yolk vs cell) (Carrington et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a speculative inference about factors that might affect editing efficiency, referencing another study.

claim: Zhao et al., 2020 showed similar efficiencies as obtained in this study.
source: More recently, Zhao et al., 2020 have shown similar efficiencies as we obtained in our study.
evidence: This statement references another study for comparison, supported by citation.

claim: The study provides a direct comparison of BE4-gam, ancBE4max, and Spymac-ancBE4max.
